task.name: run_sprint's execution state has a name but no members, so every closure still captures the frame and extraction still costs the parameter threading the state was meant to end
task.story_text:
## Why

#2325 named the sprint's execution state and did not move anything into it, so the condition it
existed to remove is still in place.

What that issue delivered is real and stays: cost accumulation and the sprint stop condition each
have exactly one owner (`SprintCostLedger`, `SprintStopCondition`), and both `nonlocal` writes into
the frame are gone. Those criteria were precisely stated and precisely met.

The third thing it asked for was that the state `run_sprint` holds in its frame be reachable by name.
That was satisfied by declaring `SprintExecutionState` — ten fields, twenty-seven lines, no methods —
which is reachable, constructible and assertable, and which changed nothing about the frame. On
merged `main` today:

| | ADR-0008 | after #2325 |
|---|---|---|
| `run_sprint` parameters | 16 | 18 |
| functions nested in `run_sprint` | 33 | 35 |
| distinct names assigned in the frame | 438 | 456 |
| the five closures ADR-0008 names by name | all nested | all still nested |

ADR-0008 states the cost this was meant to remove: *"Moving any one of them out today means
threading five to fifteen parameters to the new home, which is how the 16-parameter signature on
`run_sprint` arose in the first place."* That is still true, so every later unit the ADR sequenced
behind this one is still blocked, and the module grew by 308 lines paying for an option that was not
bought.

The criterion is therefore not that the state has a name. It is that a closure can leave.

## Example

The invariant, stated as the shape a relocated function has to have. Today `_resolve_queued_pr` is
nested because it reads a dozen values out of the enclosing frame. Moving it currently means passing
those values one at a time, which is the parameter threading this issue exists to end:

```
today
  def run_sprint(...18 params...):
      state = SprintExecutionState(...10 fields...)
      def _resolve_queued_pr():          # nested: captures ~12 frame locals
          ...
      def _attempt_integration():        # nested: captures more of the same
          ...

wanted
  def _resolve_queued_pr(state: SprintExecutionState, story: Story) -> PrResolution:
      ...                                # module scope; reads the state, not its members

  def run_sprint(context: SprintRunContext) -> SprintResult:
      state = SprintExecutionState.for_run(context)
      ...
```

The test is mechanical rather than aesthetic: after this lands, no function nested inside
`run_sprint` closes over a value the execution state carries. Anything still nested is nested by
preference, and can be moved later without re-deciding anything — which is what "every subsequent
extraction is comparatively cheap" has to mean to be checkable.

## Acceptance criteria

- The five closures ADR-0008 names — `_attempt_integration`, `_persist_current_story_result`,
  `_record_dropped_story_audit`, `_resolve_queued_pr`, `_service_plan_gates` — are defined at module
  scope rather than inside `run_sprint`.
- No function that remains nested inside `run_sprint` closes over a value carried by the execution
  state. Functions may remain nested; capturing state through the frame is what may not remain, so
  any later extraction is a move rather than a re-decision.
- No parameter of a function relocated by this change is a value the execution state carries. A
  relocated function takes the state itself plus its own per-call inputs; passing members of the
  state individually is the condition being removed and does not satisfy this.
- `run_sprint` accepts the run context rather than its individual fields, and its signature is at
  most three parameters. `SprintRunContext` already carries seventeen of the eighteen values it takes
  today.
- A test asserts the second and third criteria directly against the parsed module, so a later change
  that reintroduces frame capture or member-passing fails rather than being noticed by inspection.
- Sprint behaviour is unchanged: for the same inputs, the same stories run, in the same batches, with
  the same outcomes, costs and recorded audit fields.

## Already satisfied by #2325 — do not redo

`SprintCostLedger` and `SprintStopCondition` own cost accumulation and the stop condition, are the
only writers of each, and both `nonlocal` writes are gone. Verified on merged `main`. A change that
reopens either ownership decision is out of scope for this issue.

## Out of scope

Splitting `sprint/runner.py` into multiple modules, and reducing any module below
`max_module_lines`. ADR-0008 sequences both behind this unit. The line count may not fall as a result
of this issue, and that is expected — but note that #2325 grew the module by 308 lines, so a second
increase of that size without the frame capture being removed would mean the sequencing argument has
failed twice and should be re-examined rather than paid a third time.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
